message.content:
The reflection matrix across a line making angle \(\theta\) with the \(x\)-axis is

\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos 2\theta & \sin 2\theta \\
\sin 2\theta & -\cos 2\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Comparing with

\[
\begin{pmatrix}
-\frac{7}{25} & \frac{24}{25} \\
\frac{24}{25} & \frac{7}{25}
\end{pmatrix},
\]

we get

\[
\cos 2\theta = -\frac{7}{25}, \qquad \sin 2\theta = \frac{24}{25}.
\]

Let \(t=\tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}\). Using

\[
\tan 2\theta=\frac{\sin 2\theta}{\cos 2\theta}
=\frac{24/25}{-7/25}=-\frac{24}{7},
\]

and

\[
\tan 2\theta=\frac{2t}{1-t^2},
\]

we have

\[
\frac{2t}{1-t^2}=-\frac{24}{7}.
\]

Solving:

\[
14t=-24(1-t^2)
\]

\[
14t=-24+24t^2
\]

\[
24t^2-14t-24=0
\]

\[
12t^2-7t-12=0.
\]

Using the quadratic formula,

\[
t=\frac{7\pm 25}{24}.
\]

Thus

\[
t=\frac{32}{24}=\frac{4}{3}
\quad\text{or}\quad
t=\frac{-18}{24}=-\frac{3}{4}.
\]

Since \(\sin 2\theta>0\) and \(\cos 2\theta<0\), \(2\theta\) is in quadrant II, so \(\theta\) is in quadrant I. Hence \(\tan\theta>0\).

Therefore,

\[
\frac{y}{x}=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

The answer is \(\frac{4}{3}\).
